note: One correction: Naqada's 40 km Nile band round the Early Dynastic state's strip in Upper Egypt, the Faiyum and the Giza reach goes to nobody at -3100 (the review replaced the window agent's gain of the band by the Early Dynastic state, which that state's -3000 keyframe undid as a 124-cell snap). The Matruh/Giza desert block of Naqada is cut by the keyframe override of m3200-m3101 (naqada-culture_-3200 runs to -3000).

region.text: the Nile valley of Upper Egypt north of the First Cataract (24 N) within 40 km of the river, with the Faiyum and the Giza reach of the valley: the band round the Early Dynastic state's Cliopatria strip that Naqada still held; the valley itself, with Abydos, Naqada, Hierakonpolis, Elephantine, Memphis and the Faiyum town, is already the unified state's

events.note: Replaces the reviewer-withdrawn gain of early-dynastic-period-of-egypt (same region, same year): that gain gave the unified state 124 desert-edge cells which its own reviewed keyframe early-dynastic-period-of-egypt_-3000 ('ok', the Cliopatria strip, 93,286 km2 'from Elephantine to the coast') takes back as a 124-cell snap in -3000. The Naqada culture page: 'A 2013 study places the end circa 3,100 BC' of a culture dated 'c. 4000-3000 BC', 'Followed by: First Dynasty of Egypt'. The Early Dynastic page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Dynastic_Period_(Egypt)): the period 'immediately follows the unification of Upper and Lower Egypt in c. 3150 BC', when Narmer 'merged both the Kingdom of Upper and Lower Egypt under his single rule', 'lasting from the end of the archaeological culture of Naqada III'. The valley is already the unified state's (its -3150 keyframe); Naqada's 40 km band round it is dropped so the two no longer draw as stripes along the Nile, and the flanks are nobody's as they are from -3000 on. The unification itself is c. 3150 BC, in the window before, where the stripes remain.
